summary: 袋狼曾广布澳大利亚，后来仅存于塔斯马尼亚，最终被宣布灭绝。文章以动物学家的目击报告和多次搜寻为线索，比较支持其幸存的猜想、专家的怀疑，以及核查记录时的困难。
logic: 回顾袋狼的分布与衰退
再看长期未证实的记录

paragraphs.brief: 塔斯马尼亚虎或甲状腺，是食肉性哺乳动物(用袋装的肉食哺乳动物)。
sentences: The Tasmanian tiger, or thylacine, was a carnivorous marsupial (a meat-eating mammal which carries its young in a pouch).
塔斯马尼亚虎或甲状腺，是食肉性哺乳动物(用袋装的肉食哺乳动物)。
It was given the name ‘tiger’ because it had striped fur, and because it was ferocious.
它被命名为 " 老虎 "，因为它有条纹毛皮，而且凶猛。
Between 24 million and 15 million years ago, many types of thylacine roamed across Australia, their powerful jaws playing a role in maintaining a balance in the ecosystems of their day.
2400万到1500万年前，许多类型的甲状腺在澳大利亚漫游，他们的强力下巴在维持当今生态系统的平衡方面发挥了作用。
Some species were fox-sized, while others were barely the size of kittens.
有些物种是狐狸大小的，而其他物种则几乎与小猫一样大小。

paragraphs.brief: 但是当大约1200万年前，当一个时期的气候变化冷却了澳大利亚时，这些古老的胸腺的数量开始下降。
sentences: But when a period of climate change cooled Australia about 12 million years ago, the numbers of these ancient thylacines began to decline.
但是当大约1200万年前，当一个时期的气候变化冷却了澳大利亚时，这些古老的胸腺的数量开始下降。
By about 3 million years ago, only one species was left.
大约300万年前，只剩下一个物种。
About 4,000 years ago, these vanished completely from the Australian mainland, so that Tasmania, a large island to the south of Australia, became the last remaining place where thylacines existed.
大约在4000年前，这些植物从澳大利亚大陆完全消失，因此，澳大利亚南部的一个大岛塔斯马尼亚岛，成为了最后留下的百草枯存在的地方。
They ruled the island’s animal life unchallenged until Europeans—with sheep, dogs and a great indifference to native flora and fauna—seem to have brought about their extinction.
他们统治了该岛的动物生活，没有受到任何质疑，直到欧洲人 — — 绵羊、狗和对当地动植物的漠不关心 — — 似乎使他们灭绝。
In 1936, the last captive Tasmanian tiger died in Hobart Zoo.
1936年最后一个被俘的塔斯马尼亚老虎死在霍巴特动物园
Since then, many expeditions have searched for tigers in the Tasmanian bush, but no definitive evidence has been found.
从那时起，许多探险者在塔斯马尼亚丛林寻找老虎，但没有发现确凿的证据。
Despite this, there are many who keep searching.
尽管如此，仍然有许多人不断寻找。

paragraphs.brief: 1981年，荷兰出生的动物学家汉斯·纳丁在塔斯马尼亚对拉塔姆的狙击动物(濒危鸟类)进行了调查。
sentences: In 1981, Dutch-born zoologist Hans Naarding was in Tasmania conducting a survey of Latham’s snipe, a species of endangered bird.
1981年，荷兰出生的动物学家汉斯·纳丁在塔斯马尼亚对拉塔姆的狙击动物(濒危鸟类)进行了调查。
One night, he saw an animal in the light from the searchlight mounted on his vehicle.
一天晚上，他看到一辆汽车上安装的探照灯照着一只动物。
He described it as about the size of a large dog, but with slightly sloping hindquarters and a fairly thick tail continuing straight on from its backbone.
他把它描述成一只大狗的大小，但后部稍有倾斜，脊椎直伸着一条相当厚的尾巴。
He said that it had 12 distinct stripes on its back, running down to the point where the tail began.
他说，它的背上有12条不同的条纹，跑到尾巴开始的地方。
He reported the sighting to the Director of Tasmania’s National Parks.
他向塔斯马尼亚国家公园主任报告了目击情况。
“When the news broke,” said Naarding, “I was besieged by television crews, including four or five from Japan, and others from the United Kingdom, Germany, New Zealand and South America.”
“当新闻破灭时，”Naarding说，“我被电视摄制组人员包围，其中包括来自日本的四五个人，以及来自联合王国、德国、新西兰和南美洲的其他人。”

paragraphs.brief: 政府和私人搜查人员对该地区进行了搜查，但没有进一步发现。
sentences: Government and private search parties combed the region, but no further sightings were made.
政府和私人搜查人员对该地区进行了搜查，但没有进一步发现。
The tiger, as always, had escaped to its lair—a place that many insist exists only in the imagination.
老虎一如既往地逃到它的巢穴——许多人坚持说只有想象力才存在的地方。
Others disagree: there have been more than 4,000 claimed sightings of the animal since it supposedly died out, and the average number of claims reported to the authorities each year is now 150.
另一些人则不同意：自动物据称死亡以来，有4,000多人声称看到动物，每年向当局报告的平均要求数量现在为150件。
So is it out there?
外面有吗？
Even experts differ in opinion.
即使是专家也意见不一。

paragraphs.brief: 环保学家们一致认为，任何人口不足1000的动物都将在60年内灭绝。
sentences: Randolph Rose, Associate Professor of Zoology at the University of Tasmania, says that he once dreamed of seeing a thylacine, but is now convinced that his dream will go unfulfilled.
塔斯马尼亚大学动物学副教授Randolph Rose说，他曾经梦想看到胸膜，但现在深信他的梦想将无法实现。
The consensus among conservationists is that any animal with a population base of less than 1,000 is headed for extinction within 60 years.
环保学家们一致认为，任何人口不足1000的动物都将在60年内灭绝。
“Sixty years ago,” he says, “there was only one thylacine that we know of, and that was in Hobart Zoo.
他说，“六年前，我们所知道的只有一根百草枯，那是在霍巴特动物园。
Take it from me, the tiger is gone.”
从我这里拿走，老虎不见了。”

But Dr David Pemberton, curator of zoology at the Tasmanian Museum, states that, despite scientific thinking that a relatively large population is required to sustain a species, “the Florida panther is down to a dozen or so animals, and, while it does have some inbreeding problems, it’s still ticking along!
但塔斯马尼亚博物馆动物学馆长大卫·彭贝顿博士指出，尽管科学上认为需要大量人口来养活一个物种，“佛罗里达豹体已经下降到十几只左右，虽然它确实有一些传宗接代的问题，它仍然在不停地前进!
After all, animals can be notoriously elusive.
毕竟，动物是臭名昭著的难以捉摸。

The strange fish known as the coelacanth, with its ‘proto legs,’ was thought to have died out with the dinosaurs 700 million years ago, until a specimen was dragged to the surface in a shark net off the coast of South Africa in 1938.”
这种长着“原始腿”的奇鱼叫作腔棘鱼。原以为它在 7 亿年前与恐龙一同灭绝，直到 1938 年，南非沿海的一张捕鲨网把一条腔棘鱼带出了水面。

paragraphs.brief: " 在面值上，穆尼说，" 这个关于目光和作为证据提交的照片的具体描述，就我所看到的物种生存的最有说服力的例子之一。
sentences: Wildlife biologist Nick Mooney has the unenviable task of investigating all so-called sightings of the tiger.
野生动物生物学家尼克·穆尼承担着调查所有所谓的老虎目击的不可饶恕的任务
It was Mooney who was first consulted in late February 2005 about the authenticity of new digital photographic images of a thylacine allegedly taken by a tourist.
2005年2月底，莫尼首次被问及据称由一名游客拍摄的一幅甲状腺新数字照片的真实性。
“On face value,” Mooney says, “this particular account of a sighting and the photographs submitted as proof amount to one of the most convincing cases for the species’ survival that I have seen.”
" 在面值上，穆尼说，" 这个关于目光和作为证据提交的照片的具体描述，就我所看到的物种生存的最有说服力的例子之一。
Many other ‘sightings’ have been hoaxes, and many sincere seekers are victims of obsession.
许多真诚的追求者都是痴迷的受害者。
“It is a blind optimism that something is, rather than cynicism that something isn’t,” Mooney says.
穆尼说：“这是一种盲目的乐观，宁愿相信某件事确实存在，也不愿以愤世嫉俗的态度断定它不存在。”
“If something crosses the road, it’s not a case of ‘I wonder what that was?’
" 如果有东西越过了这条路，那不是`我想知道那是什么？' 的例子。
Rather, it is a case of ‘That’s a thylacine!’”
更确切地说，这是一个"这是胸膜!"

paragraphs.brief: 但是，穆尼对待所有的目光面值。
sentences: However, Mooney treats all sightings at face value.
但是，穆尼对待所有的目光面值。
“I never try to embarrass people,” he says, “but the fact that I don’t pack the car immediately after they telephone can often be taken as ridicule.
“我从来不试图让别人难堪，”他说，“但是，在他们打电话后，我不立即打包汽车，这往往会被当作嘲笑。
Obsessive characters get angry that someone in my position is not out there when they think the thylacine is there.”
偏执的人物会生气像我这样的人以为胸膜就在那里时就不会在外面

paragraphs.brief: 如果那里有胸腺，那么在他们所在的地方就更好了。”
sentences: Hans Naarding, whose sighting of a striped animal two decades ago was the highlight of a lifetime of animal spotting, remains puzzled by the time and money people waste on tiger searches.
Hans Naarding 20年前看到一条条纹动物成为了动物一生的发现却被时间和金钱浪费在老虎的搜索上令他困惑不解
He says resources would be better applied to saving another endangered animal, the Tasmanian devil, and helping declining migratory bird populations.
他说资源会更好地用于拯救另一个濒危动物，塔斯马尼亚魔鬼，并帮助减少迁徙鸟类数量。
Could the thylacine still be out there?
胸膜还在外面吗？
“Sure,” Naarding says.
“当然，”Naarding说。
“I know the vast south-west wilderness of Tasmania well.
“我对塔斯马尼亚西南大片荒野很了解。
They could survive … [But] if this is the case, it will not be long before they do disappear completely.”
他们可以活下来... 但是，如果是这样的话，不久他们就会完全消失。
Naarding believes that any discovery of surviving thylacines would be “rather pointless.”
Naarding认为任何发现幸存的甲状腺将“毫无意义”。
“How do you bring a species back from extinction?” he asks.
他问：“你如何使一种物种从灭绝中恢复过来？”
“What could you do with it?
“你能用它做什么？
If there are thylacines out there, they are better off right where they are.”
如果那里有胸腺，那么在他们所在的地方就更好了。”

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词，可含数字。

items.en: There is no longer any hope of finding a surviving Tasmanian tiger.
items.zh: 已经没有希望找到一个幸存的塔斯马尼亚老虎了

items.en: It would be preferable not to disturb any surviving Tasmanian tigers.
items.zh: 最好不要打扰任何幸存的塔斯马尼亚老虎。

items.en: Many who claim to have seen Tasmanian tigers are not objective witnesses.
items.zh: 许多自称见过塔斯马尼亚老虎的人不是客观的证人。

items.en: Expert estimates of numbers needed to ensure species survival may be inaccurate.
items.zh: 专家对确保物种生存所需的数字估计可能不准确。

items.en: There is a great deal of international interest in Tasmanian tiger stories.
items.zh: 国际上对塔斯马尼亚老虎的故事很感兴趣。

clauses: 连接词 because 引出“because it had striped fur, and because it was ferocious”，说明主句的原因关系。

连接词 while 引出“while others were barely the size of kittens”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
